A BA2 header is 24 bytes: magic BTDX, u32 version, 4-char type GNRL or DX10, u32 file count, u64 name-table offset. Every installed archive parses with this layout.

BA2 versions 7 and 8 use the version 1 record layout for both GNRL and DX10; all 643 installed archives parse and inflate a sampled entry with that layout (assumption A7 confirmed).

BA2 name and directory hashes are CRC-32 (reflected 0xEDB88320) with initial value 0 and no final XOR over the lowercase file stem and the lowercase backslash directory; 504352 of 504355 vanilla entries match (3 DLC entries carry names that differ from what was hashed).

facts.claim: Vanilla GNRL archives never compress .pex, .fuz, .wav, .xwm, .strings/.dlstrings/.ilstrings, .swf, .gfx, .png, .xml or .dds; meshes, materials, text and havok files are mostly zlib-compressed. The forge writer stores the never-compressed list and compresses the rest when that shrinks the file.
facts.source: per-extension packed/stored counts over the vanilla archives

facts.claim: Every vanilla GNRL record carries flags 0x00100100 and alignment marker 0xBAADF00D.

DX10 chunk layout: a mip gets its own chunk while it has at least 512x512 pixels (262144), up to 3 single-mip chunks; the remaining mips share the last chunk (4 chunks at most); cubemaps are one chunk. Matches all 41077 vanilla DX10 entries and Archive2's own defaults (-maxChunkCount 4, -singleMipChunkX/Y 512). DX10 records: unknown byte 0, chunk header size 24, flags 0x800 (0x801 cubemap).

The forge writer repacked Fallout4 - Materials.ba2 (6899 files, GNRL v1) and Fallout4 - TexturesPatch.ba2 (7 files, DX10 v1): names, payload hashes and DX10 chunk layout equal the originals, texdiag accepts all 7 re-extracted DDS, and Archive2 1.1.0.5 extracts both forge-written archives with identical payload hashes. In-game load: NOT RUN.
facts.source: T12 round trip, report under the forge home reports/t12-ba2-roundtrip.json
facts.how: f4forge ba2 extract + f4forge ba2 pack + Archive2 -extract

facts.claim: Fallout 4 light plugins hold new object IDs up to 0xFFF. The floor is 0x001 when the plugin's HEDR version is at least 1.0 and it has at least one master (the 'hardcoded range' xEdit admits for FO4), otherwise 0x800. The same floor applies to new records in full plugins.
facts.source: xEdit dev-4.1.6 commit ee216dfac1e191a6ea821fbc3e492f8fb37b5a56, https://github.com/TES5Edit/TES5Edit/blob/ee216dfac1e191a6ea821fbc3e492f8fb37b5a56/Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas (gdHardcodedRangeAdmitted/MinVersion 1.0) and Core/wbImplementation.pas GetAllowHardcodedRangeUseByGeneration; MaxObjectID $FFF in Core/wbInterface.pas

facts.claim: All 188 installed .esl files pass the light-range check (182 HEDR 1.0 with IDs from 0x001, 6 HEDR 0.95 from 0x800).

The HEDR record count is not the number of records: Fallout4.esm declares 1741853 while a full walk finds 1549276 records in 112381 groups (56399 compressed). DLCCoast.esm declares 320320 and holds 309239 records in 11081 groups.
facts.source: plugin walk of the official masters

facts.claim: HEDR 1.0 plugins are what the Next-Gen and later runtimes and Creation Kit 1.11 produce; older runtimes expect 0.95.
facts.source: installed CC .esl files and Fallout4.esm carry 1.0 on the 1.11.240 runtime; older-runtime behaviour not tested

facts.claim: This install loads 552 plugins: 7 official masters, 173 Creation Club plugins and 372 starred plugins.txt entries (115 full, 437 light), with no missing files or masters.
FO4Edit's own Nexus page is fallout4/mods/2737.

Fallout 4 PEX files are little-endian (magic bytes DE C0 57 FA, version 3.9, game id 2); Skyrim's are big-endian. After the header and string table come debug info (functions, then Fallout 4 property groups and struct orders), user flags and objects (name index, u32 size including itself, parent class index first).
facts.source: Champollion source https://github.com/Orvid/Champollion/blob/bc961a0bdfb4831f8240e6dacee0818b4bf81e00/Pex/FileReader.cpp; confirmed on vanilla scripts\Actor.pex from Fallout4 - Misc.ba2

facts.claim: The Creation Kit's Institute_Papyrus_Flags.flg defines Hidden 0, Conditional 1, Default 2, CollapsedOnRef 3, CollapsedOnBase 4, Collapsed = CollapsedOnRef & CollapsedOnBase, Mandatory 5. The forge ships its own F4Forge_Papyrus_Flags.flg with the same names and indexes.

F4SE's source keeps only the additions in scripts/modified/*.psc; its build appends each to the vanilla script of the same name (F4SE.psc is complete). Using scripts/modified directly as an import fails to parse.

Base.zip extracts 7857 .psc and DLC01-DLC06.zip 483/44/831/909/41/93 into a DLC0x namespace folder each; ScriptObject, Form, Actor and Quest are present. One official test script (TestKevinActivationScript.psc) indents its ScriptName line, which Caprica cannot read; the cache copy is patched.

PapyrusCompiler 2.8.0.4 reports 'file.psc(line,col): message'; Caprica 0.3.0 reports 'file.psc (line, col:endcol): Fatal Error: message'. Both compile a Quest script that calls Debug.Trace and F4SE.GetVersion against the official + merged F4SE sources, and both turn a planted syntax error into one structured diagnostic with exit 1. Caprica scans import folders recursively and reads 'Parent' as a keyword (F4SE's ConnectPoint.parent struct member), handled by a Caprica-only overlay.

Champollion 1.3.2 decompiled a 50-entry sample of game .pex (49 unique scripts) with 0 failures; every decompiled ScriptName/extends pair equals the official source. Compiling against a full decompiled import set has not been run (assumption A2 partly open).

Vanilla texture formats by suffix: _d BC1_UNORM (6294) or BC3_UNORM with alpha (3155); _n BC5_UNORM (5071 of 5644); _s BC5_UNORM (6281 of 6885); _msn BC3/BC1; _g BC1; _e BC1 or B8G8R8A8. All 41077 vanilla DX10 textures are power-of-two and 40901 carry a full mip chain (single-mip exceptions are tint masks). Vanilla uses UNORM, not sRGB, formats.
facts.source: every DX10 entry of Fallout4 - Textures*.ba2 and DLC texture archives
facts.how: f4forge tex inspect <dds> / f4forge ba2 list <texture archive>

facts.claim: BGSM/BGEM layout (field order, version conditions, u32-length null-terminated strings, colors as three floats) follows Material-Editor's MaterialLib; reading and writing all 6899 materials of Fallout4 - Materials.ba2 (BGSM v2 6616, BGEM v2 283) is byte-identical, and all 26081 binary materials in the 261 installed archives that carry materials round-trip byte-identically (versions 0-3).
The game also reads JSON-text materials: vanilla Fallout4 - Startup.ba2 ships 5 interface .BGEM files as JSON, and 46 JSON materials exist across installed archives.
facts.source: material sweep of the installed archives

facts.claim: Fallout 4 meshes are NIF 20.2.0.7, user version 12, BS version 130, with author, process script, export script and max-filepath export strings, block types, per-block sizes, a string table (material paths live there) and a root-list footer; texture paths sit in BSShaderTextureSet blocks.
facts.source: niftools nif.xml https://github.com/niftools/nifxml/blob/develop/nif.xml (Header, BSStreamHeader); confirmed on vanilla Meshes\SetDressing\MetalBarrel\MetalBarrel01.nif

facts.claim: PyNifly 30.3.0 runs in headless Blender 5.3 when enabled with addon_utils from its tools folder (preferences not saved); a plain register() fails because the add-on reads its own preferences. Export returns an empty set on success, so the written file is the evidence. A vanilla static (MetalBarrel01) imports, exports as FO4 and parses again (8 blocks, references resolved).
FUZ = 'FUZE', u32 version 1, u32 LIP size, LIP bytes, then the xWMA audio (RIFF XWMA). Vanilla voice audio is xWMA mono 44100 Hz.
Voice files live at Sound\Voice\<Plugin>\<VoiceType>\<INFO FormID, 8 hex>_<response>.fuz; 114035 of 116101 entries in Fallout4 - Voices.ba2 follow this pattern.
Voice WAV input: 16-bit PCM mono (vanilla voice audio is mono 44100 Hz); xwmaencode accepts bitrates 20000-192000 (default 48000).
facts.source: vanilla FUZ audio header; xwmaencode.exe usage text
